name: Deng Xiaoping
description: Chinese leader who promoted economic reform and opening while maintaining Communist Party political control.
scope: Public positions and conduct during the specified period; this represents the individual rather than all party members or citizens.

axes.brief: The Four Cardinal Principles preserved Communist Party rule and rejected competitive pluralism.
axes.counter: Internal consultations and institutional reform differed from personal unlimited rule.

axes.brief: Dissent suppression and party security constrained civil liberties.
axes.counter: Economic liberalisation did not produce equivalent political liberalisation.

axes.brief: National unity and common institutions coexisted with recognised ethnic minorities.
axes.counter: Regional minority recognition did not provide unrestricted cultural autonomy.

axes.brief: Controlled settlement and national sovereignty provide restrictive migration context.
axes.counter: Opening to investment and foreigners is distinct from permanent immigration rights.

axes.brief: The Vietnam war and military modernisation showed readiness to use force.
axes.counter: Later development priorities and pragmatic diplomacy limited continuous military expansion.

axes.brief: Sovereignty and non-interference coexisted with global economic opening.
axes.counter: Trade integration did not imply supranational political or monetary authority.

axes.brief: State enterprises remained while private, collective and foreign firms expanded.
axes.counter: Reform did not establish a general commitment to privatising strategic assets.

axes.brief: Special economic zones and foreign investment opened trade selectively.
axes.counter: National controls and protected strategic sectors prevent an unrestricted free-trade reading.

axes.brief: Market incentives and decollectivisation coexisted with state plans and financial direction.
axes.counter: Neither the earlier Maoist command system nor fully free markets describe this period.

axes.brief: Allowing some people to prosper first accepted income differences during development.
axes.counter: Common prosperity and public social institutions remained stated goals.

axes.brief: Civil party-state institutions controlled religious activity without clerical legal authority.
axes.counter: Restored religious practice did not create an official religious foundation.

axes.brief: Gender participation and socialist family reform coexisted with coercive family planning.
axes.counter: Forced reproductive policy is distinct from voluntary abortion’s social acceptance.

axes.brief: The Four Modernisations prioritised science, industry and technical development.
axes.counter: Modern gene-enhancement risk thresholds remain analogical estimates.

axes.brief: National party control coexisted with substantial provincial economic experimentation.
axes.counter: Economic delegation is not a constitutional regional right to resist or secede.

reasons.6: Provincial and local fiscal incentives and experimentation were important to reform. National political supremacy does not by itself determine this specific revenue-retention choice.

axes.brief: Education, modernisation and changing incentives supplied accounts of improved conduct and productivity.
axes.counter: Specific inherited comparisons are not established by economic reform.
axes.gap: These are especially uncertain causal estimates; socialist education and incentives are contextual evidence rather than a complete heredity doctrine.
